chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdallah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding His words:

He said: It means the encompassing of imagination (al-wahm). Do you not see His words: 'There have come to you insights (basair) from your Lord'? He does not mean the sight of the eyes. 'Whosoever sees (absara) then it will be for his own self' — He does not mean by 'see' through the eye. 'And whoever is blind is against it' — He does not mean the blindness of the eyes. He means the encompassing of imagination, as it is said: So-and-so is insightful (basir) in poetry, and so-and-so is insightful in jurisprudence, and so-and-so is insightful in coins, and so-and-so is insightful in clothes. Allah is greater than to be seen by the eye.

key_terms.الْأَبْصَارُ: Sights (plural of baseerah, referring to vision or perception)
key_terms.بَصِيرٌ: Insightful or knowledgeable in a specific field

ai.seo_question: What does 'sights do not reach Him' mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'sights' (absar) in the verse refers to the faculty of imagination (wahm) and intellectual perception rather than physical eyesight, supported by the linguistic usage of 'basir' to denote expertise in fields like jurisprudence. This interpretation aligns with the Shia theological principle of tanzih, emphasizing that God’s essence is beyond the grasp of human sensory or conceptual faculties. The Imam concludes that since Allah is too great to be seen by the eyes, He is also beyond the reach of human imagination.

en.ammaar-muslim: 5. [5/324] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from Ibn Abi Najran from Abdallah b. Sinan from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام about His words:

- he (the Imam) said: (It means) comprehension by the imagination (is impossible for Him). Do you not see His words: “There have come to you insights (Basair) from your Lord” [6:104] - He does not mean sighting of the eyes. “Whosoever will see (Absara) then it will be for his own self” [6:104] - He does not mean by (the word) ‘see’ through his eye. “and whoever is blind is against it” [6:104] - He does not mean the blindness of the eyes. He means comprehension by the imagination - as is said: So-and-so is insightful (Basir) in poetry, So-and-so is insightful in jurisprudence, So-and-so is insightful in coins (telling forgeries from the real thing), So-and-so is insightful in clothes. Allah is greater than to be seen by the eye.
